subject: mathematics_1b
question_text: Find dy and Δy for y = 1/(x + 2) when x = 8 and Δx = 0.02.

mark_split.label: Find Δy from the exact change

recall_prompt: Say how you would do this one — say how you get dy, and say what makes Δy a different number.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Find dy from the derivative
steps.margin_note: First mark. The derivative is negative, so dy is negative too. Keep the minus sign — dropping it is the commonest way this mark is lost.

recall.must_convey: That dy/dx = −1/(x + 2)², which is −1/100 at x = 8, so dy = −0.0002.
accept: differentiate one over x plus two to get minus one over x plus two squared
at x equals eight the derivative is minus one by hundred
d y is minus zero point zero zero zero two
derivative minus one by hundred vasthundi, delta x tho multiply cheyyali
the answer is negative because y decreases as x increases
heard_as: minus zero point zero zero zero two

steps.why: 1/(x + 2) is (x + 2)⁻¹, and the power rule gives −(x + 2)⁻², so the derivative is negative everywhere the function is defined. That sign is part of the answer, not a slip.
common_mistakes: Writing dy/dx = 1/(x + 2)² without the minus sign.
Squaring only x instead of the whole bracket (x + 2).
steps.memory_tip: dy uses the derivative once. Δy uses the function twice. d for derivative, Δ for difference.

steps.label: Find Δy from the exact change
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Subtracting the two fractions over a common denominator, 10.02 × 10 = 100.2, is faster and safer than converting each one to a decimal first.

accept: delta y is one by ten point zero two minus one by ten
take the common denominator hundred point two
the exact change is minus zero point zero zero zero one nine nine six
both d y and delta y are negative
heard_as: one by ten point zero two
minus zero point zero zero zero one nine nine six

steps.why: Δy is the real change in y, so the function is worked out at both points. Both numbers are negative because y falls as x rises here, and they agree to six decimal places, which is why dy is a usable stand-in for Δy.
common_mistakes: Rounding 1/10.02 to 0.0998 and getting Δy = −0.0002 exactly, which hides the difference the question asks about.
Reporting Δy as positive after subtracting in the wrong order.
steps.memory_tip: Δy is the after value minus the before value, in that order — a negative Δy is allowed and simply means y went down.

insider_note: The derivative is NEGATIVE, so both dy and Δy come out negative — the function is decreasing. Losing that sign is the standard error here.
